title: Crond
subtitle: cron daemon, crontab sources, five-field syntax, and schedule patterns — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: The daemon that executes scheduled commands
cards.notes: Memory hook: cron = the clock daemon. On systemd usually crond.service / cron.service.

cards.meaning: The table of jobs (that user’s schedule file)
cards.notes: Edit with crontab -e, not a random text file, unless you are an admin on the system files.

cards.meaning: Each minute — runs jobs whose fields match this minute
User crontab files, named after accounts in /etc/passwd; loaded into memory (Red Hat / CentOS)
cards.notes: Debian/Ubuntu often /var/spool/cron/crontabs. You can edit by hand; crontab is the supported way.

cards.meaning: Anacron table — different format; jobs that should still run if the machine was off
Extra system drop-in files; different format from user crontabs — includes a user field
System-wide crontab; same format as /etc/cron.d/ (username after five time fields)
Mailed to the crontab owner, or to MAILTO if that variable is set
cards.notes: With cron -s, job output can also go to syslog.

cards.meaning: Edit the current user’s crontab in $EDITOR
Edit someone else’s crontab (needs privilege)
Drop a script; it runs on that cadence via a system cron/anacron hook — no five-field line
cards.notes: Memory hook: cron.daily = just put a script in the folder.

cards.meaning: minute hour day-of-month month weekday, then the command
cards.notes: Memory hook: min hour dom month dow.

cards.meaning: 1–12 or jan, feb, …
0–7; 0 and 7 = Sunday; names like sun work
After the five time fields in /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.d/
cards.notes: User crontabs do not have this field.

cards.meaning: Every value of that field
5 and 17
Every 10 of that field (minutes, hours, …)
02:00 every day
05:00 and 17:00 every day
Every minute (at second 0)
Every Sunday at 17:00
Every 10 minutes
Every minute in January, May, and August
17:00 on Sunday and Friday
First Sunday of the month at 02:00 (Sundays only if date is 1–7)
cards.notes: Cron cannot say first Sunday alone. 0 2 * * sun is every Sunday; the date test keeps days 1–7.

cards.meaning: Every four hours, on the hour
04:00 and 17:00 on Sunday and Monday
Two lines: the job at second 0, and sleep 30; same job
cards.notes: Cron has no sub-minute scheduling. Sub-minute = sleep.

cards.meaning: Two commands in one minute slot
/etc/rc.d/init.d or /etc/init.d
